problem: State set is listed as a node type, but in OpenSceneGraph osg::StateSet is not a node. It is a state attribute container attached to a node's drawables or to a group; the node types are Group, Transform (MatrixTransform/PositionAttitudeTransform) and Geode.
fix: Nodes include group, transform and geode; render state such as material and texture is held in a state set attached to those nodes.

where: Lead and Section 1, definition of scene graph
problem: The chapter says a scene graph is a tree only. Most toolkits (OpenSceneGraph and most engines) let one node be shared by several parents, so the structure is really a directed acyclic graph, and that sharing is how instancing is done. A student who reads only 'tree' will not recognise a shared subtree.
fix: A scene graph is a tree or directed acyclic graph of nodes: usually a tree, but a node can be shared by more than one parent to instance the same geometry.

problem: The answer suggests a child cannot get its world transform without depth-first order, but a breadth-first walk level by level also knows every parent transform before its children. Depth-first is chosen because a stack naturally pushes and pops transforms and render state on the way down and back up.
fix: Answer: depth-first traversal matches the hierarchy; the toolkit pushes a parent's transform and state on the way down and pops them on the way back up, so each child is drawn with the correct combined transform and state without recomputing from the root.

problem: T_T is described as 'the transform of T, M's parent'. In a deeper tree that is ambiguous: what multiplies p_local is the accumulated transform from the root down to T, not T's own local transform. The example is correct only because the root is identity and T has a single translation.
fix: p_world = T_T × T_M × p_local, where T_T is the world transform of T (the product of all transforms from the root down to T) and T_M is M's local transform.
